experiment.answers: the shape sweep's own claim boundary -- 'width is a SECOND AXIS THIS SWEEP DOES NOT COVER'

headline: The shape sweep named width as the axis it did not cover. Sweeping it found the kernels width-robust -- 42 configurations, 336 executions, zero wrong. THE RESULT THAT MATTERS IS THE POSITIVE CONTROL'S: a barrier stripped from AirNorm is caught 8 of 8 runs at threadgroups 64 through 1024 AND IS EXACT AT 32, because there the whole threadgroup is ONE SIMDGROUP and lockstep makes the fence unnecessary. A control run only at 32 would have reported the broken kernel fine.
why_width_is_not_shape: a shape-dependent defect is DETERMINISTIC -- wrong every run at the wrong shape, which is why 2885 single runs settled it. A width-dependent one is usually a RACE and therefore PROBABILISTIC: the top-k barrier fired in 16 of 30 runs at 1024 and 0 of 30 at 256. So this sweep REPEATS, and its resolving power comes from the repeat count rather than the width list.

the_sweep.reading: the write-after-read the normalization block fixed structurally in norm, softmax and attention does not reappear at any width, and neither does anything else

THE_POSITIVE_CONTROL_IS_THE_EVIDENCE.what_was_broken: one threadgroup_barrier removed from AirNorm's lowering
THE_POSITIVE_CONTROL_IS_THE_EVIDENCE.why_32_is_blind: a 32-wide threadgroup is exactly ONE SIMDGROUP, and this program already measured that within a simdgroup 32 lanes exchanging through threadgroup memory are exact with NO fence because lockstep makes it unnecessary. The control reproduces that finding from a completely different direction -- it was built to prove the sweep can fail, and it also proves WHERE it cannot.
THE_POSITIVE_CONTROL_IS_THE_EVIDENCE.the_error_grows_with_width: 0.427 at 64, 0.955 at 128, 1.685 at 256, 2.764 at 512, 3.273 at 1024 -- more simdgroups, more disagreement, which is the mechanism showing itself rather than a threshold
THE_POSITIVE_CONTROL_IS_THE_EVIDENCE.why_this_matters_beyond_this_kernel: a probabilistic sweep reporting zero failures is exactly the shape of a check that cannot fail, and the previous block found precisely that in its own instrument. A control is what separates 'nothing is wrong' from 'nothing was looked at'.

shipped.kernel_forge.swept_with_control: runs the real check AND a deliberately broken one over the same cases, and REFUSES the result if the broken arm passes everywhere -- not because the kernel is wrong but because the sweep proved nothing. Reports control_blind_at as a first-class field.
shipped.detection_floor_per_run: 1 - 0.5**(1/repeat), reported with every sweep, so a clean result cannot be read as proof that no race exists. At repeat=8 the sweep is blind to anything under ~8.3% per run.
shipped.kernel_forge.WIDTH_PRIOR: 32 through 1024, the legal Metal range in simdgroup steps

prediction.written: the fixed kernels are correct at all widths, and the honest limit is that N runs cannot detect a race whose per-run probability is under ~1/N
prediction.verdict: CONFIRMED on both halves, and the control added a third thing I did not predict -- that the control ITSELF has a blind width

claim_boundary.eight_runs: repeat=8 detects a race with per-run probability above ~8.3% about half the time; the top-k race at 1024 ran at 53% and would be caught, a 2% race would not. ZERO FAILURES IS NOT ABSENCE OF RACES.
claim_boundary.one_shape_per_primitive: width is varied and shape is held FIXED, the mirror of the previous sweep's boundary rather than its closure
claim_boundary.one_control: AirNorm's barrier. The control demonstrates the sweep can fail on a TOTAL dependency; the top-k receipt already showed an INCIDENTAL one is far quieter, so a control's loudness is not transferable evidence
claim_boundary.f32_one_machine: INSTANCE, and lockstep at simd width 32 remains an M3 Ultra observation not a property of Apple GPUs
